_meta.role: New College Grad, Senior Test Engineer

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, graduating May 2026, with hands-on embedded systems and hardware test experience across STM32, Jetson, and Arduino platforms. Skilled in C/C++, Python, and Linux, with experience debugging embedded systems using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and schematic-level analysis. Background spans bare-metal firmware development, sensor integration, and systematic resolution of hardware/software integration failures.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end across national-level competitions.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on a Cortex-M4; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for real-time temperature monitoring firmware.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) across a Jetson+Arduino Linux pipeline; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over I2C mux.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override on STM32.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
